evidence_basis.note: Confirms the completed one-for-one TeamID 1 ↔ TeamID 6 trade: Robert received Jaxson Dart and Tim received Harold Fannin.

Distilled from the contemporary WhatsApp export: Robert asked about Dart on Tim's bench and directly offered Fannin. Robert framed Fannin as youth for Tim's older TE group / Njoku situation. Tim accepted immediately without asking for an add-on and said his QB depth made Dart expendable.
The 2025 league configuration had two dedicated QB starter slots.
Robert acquired Harold Fannin via waiver on 2025-09-10, about six weeks before the trade.
Tim selected Jaxson Dart at 2025 Rookie 4.03 (overall pick 21).

Robert remembers Dart as especially attractive because he was a New York Giants QB, had already shown encouraging development in several NFL starts, and offered young-QB depth in the league's transition to two starting QBs.

Robert remembers Fannin as a real ascending TE asset, not disposable waiver filler, but TE was a surplus area because he had McBride, Kincaid, Warren and Loveland. He considered Fannin-for-Dart fair, felt positive when Tim accepted, but immediately wondered whether he could have offered less. Decision confidence = 4/5; outcome uncertainty = 3/5; gut feeling positive. Robert likely would not have paid materially more than Fannin, though a small late pick may still have been acceptable.

This supports the plausibility of Robert's lower-confidence recollection that Dart may have been a player he was disappointed to miss, but does not by itself prove target intent.

decision_context.objective: Acquire Jaxson Dart as a young Giants quarterback with developing NFL upside and strategic value in the league's move to two starting QBs, using surplus TE depth to make the deal.
decision_context.roster_context: Robert remembers having strong TE depth with Trey McBride, Dalton Kincaid, Tyler Warren, Colston Loveland and Harold Fannin, making TE the position from which he could afford to trade. He did not view Fannin as valueless; Fannin was already seen as an up-and-coming TE. At QB, the shift from one starter to two made accumulating young depth materially more important.
decision_context.cap_salary_context: No salary/cap rationale is preserved for this 2025 trade and none is used in the reconstruction.
decision_context.team_window: The trade was a long-term dynasty roster-construction move: convert depth at TE into a young quarterback asset with possible starting value in a two-QB environment.
decision_context.market_context: Dart had already started several NFL games and was showing developmental upside before the trade. Robert also had a personal Giants-fan preference that increased his interest. Tim had surplus quarterback depth and accepted the direct Fannin-for-Dart offer immediately.
decision_context.why_now: Dart's early NFL development had made him more interesting, while Robert's TE room could absorb the loss of Fannin. Robert wanted to add young QB depth during the league's two-QB transition rather than wait.
constraints: Fannin was considered a meaningful young asset, so Robert did not view him as a throw-in.
Robert's TE depth made Fannin movable without reopening the core TE position.
Robert likely would not have paid materially more than Fannin; at most he remembers a small late pick as possibly acceptable.
Tim's immediate acceptance created some post-offer regret that Robert may have led with more than necessary.

theses.statement: Dart's early NFL development plus the value of young quarterback depth in a two-QB dynasty format justified moving a meaningful but surplus TE asset.
falsification_conditions: Dart's early development did not translate into a realistic path to useful starting-QB value.
The league's two-QB structure did not materially increase the value of young QB depth for Robert.

theses.statement: Robert's TE depth made Fannin the right positional bridge even though Fannin himself was already viewed as an ascending player with real upside.
falsification_conditions: Moving Fannin materially weakened Robert's TE room despite McBride, Kincaid, Warren and Loveland.
Fannin was already too important to Robert's long-term TE plan to be an appropriate trade asset.

theses.statement: The one-for-one price was fair for Robert because it converted surplus positional depth into a young QB target, though Tim's immediate acceptance suggested Robert might have been able to negotiate a slightly cheaper structure.
falsification_conditions: A materially cheaper Dart acquisition path was realistically available and Robert could have identified it before offering Fannin.
Fannin's market value at the time was clearly above Dart's to a degree that made the direct swap poor value.

alternatives.description: Keep Harold Fannin and do not acquire Jaxson Dart.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert prioritized adding a young QB asset in the new two-QB environment and viewed his TE room as deep enough to move Fannin.

alternatives.description: Try to acquire Dart with a smaller asset or a cheaper package before offering Fannin.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert led with what he believed was a fair strong offer and Tim accepted immediately; Robert only afterward wondered whether he could have paid less.

price_ceiling.description: Fannin alone was already a substantial offer in Robert's view. He likely would not have paid materially more; at most a small late pick may have been acceptable.

known_risks.description: Fannin was already viewed as an ascending young TE with real upside, so Robert risked selling meaningful future value from a strong position group.
Dart had only a small NFL sample, so several encouraging starts did not eliminate substantial uncertainty about whether he would become a durable fantasy starter.
Robert's Giants fandom may have increased his willingness to target and value Dart.
Tim's immediate acceptance suggested a negotiation-process risk that Robert may have opened with more value than was strictly necessary.

decision_state_at_execution.confidence_rationale: Robert remembers being fairly sure the trade itself was the right roster move: young QB depth mattered in the new two-QB format, Dart had shown encouraging development and the TE room could absorb losing Fannin. The doubt was more about whether Fannin was a stronger opening offer than necessary than about whether to acquire Dart.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_confidence_driver: Young-QB scarcity/optionality in a two-QB league, Dart's encouraging early NFL development and Robert's ability to trade from deep TE strength.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_source_of_doubt: Dart remained an uncertain rookie outcome, and Tim's immediate acceptance made Robert wonder whether he could have acquired him for less than Fannin.
known_personal_biases: New York Giants fandom increased Robert's attraction to Dart.
Possible target attachment to a young QB who had begun showing encouraging NFL development.
